title: Native HCN2 activity is not required for normal brain patterning

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Native HCN2 activity is not required for normal brain patterning

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Because a dominant-negative HCN2 construct does not disrupt brain patterning, native HCN2 channel activity is not required for normal Xenopus brain patterning, ruling out the possibility that nicotine causes defects by directly blocking endogenous HCN2.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: HCN2 Rescues brain defects by enforcing endogenous voltage pre-patterns

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Pai VP 2018, HCN2 Rescues brain defects by enforcing endogenous voltage pre-patterns › Discussion

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: However, our experiments with dominant-negative HCN2 channel shows that native HCN2 channel activity is not required for proper brain patterning (Supplementary Figure 4), thus negating this possibility.

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Pai VP, Pietak A, Willocq V, Ye B, Shi NQ, Levin M, “HCN2 Rescues brain defects by enforcing endogenous voltage pre-patterns”, Nature communications (2018), doi:10.1038/s41467-018-03334-5; section “Discussion”. Scope: Xenopus laevis embryos injected with Hcn2-DN mRNA

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on levin-2018-hcn2-16: needs-new-data, resolvability 0.56

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The claim is testable, but inferring non-requirement from a dominant-negative null result is vulnerable to incomplete inhibition and compensation. Public resources may provide related evidence, yet the decisive validated loss-of-function and morphology records are not identified.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Compare blinded brain morphology after validated HCN2 loss of function against matched controls, while confirming channel inhibition, and test whether defect incidence and shape remain within equivalence bounds.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
No open raw loss-of-function dataset is identified.

A null phenotype cannot show dispensability unless inhibition is complete.

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The logical step from a negative DN result to 'not required' is only as strong as the functional block, which is part of the measurement. Neither the morphology counts nor an embryonic current block are in a public dataset. Other HCN family members make a single-construct negative especially hard to interpret after the fact. Resolving the claim means repeating the DN arm with a demonstrated block, which is new data.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Score brain morphology after Hcn2-DN mRNA in otherwise untreated embryos, and require evidence that the construct blocks native embryonic HCN current. Native HCN2 is dispensable if defect rates match controls despite a blocked current; a high defect rate, or a construct that never blocks current, would undermine the conclusion that nicotine cannot be acting by inhibiting endogenous HCN2.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
A negative phenotype is weak unless the dominant-negative is shown to act in the embryo.

Supplementary Figure 4 is a summary, not a deposited count table.

Xenopus has other HCN genes that a mouse HCN2-DN might miss.

fields.label: Hypothesis
fields.value: The GYG->AAA mouse HCN2 construct used in the paper can still co-assemble with wild-type HCN2 subunits (the premise that makes it dominant-negative), so that a construct which fails to disrupt patterning can be read as evidence that native HCN2 activity is not required.

fields.label: Pass criterion
fields.value: Pre-registered. Model: mouse HCN2 (UniProt O88703) residues 131-520 (assembly region, S1-S6 and C-linker). AlphaFold3 on the Nebius Scientific AI Platform predicts (a) a wild-type homotetramer, (b) a 1 AAA : 3 WT heterotetramer and (c) an AAA homotetramer. stab-ddG on the wild-type tetramer predicts the change in binding energy between chain A and chains B+C+D for G402A/Y403A/G404A on chain A. Supports the premise if ALL of: WT ipTM >= 0.60; heterotetramer ipTM >= WT ipTM - 0.10; AAA binding ddG <= 1.0 kcal/mol; and the sensitivity control (chain-A residue with the most inter-subunit heavy-atom contacts within 4 A, mutated to Arg) gives ddG >= 2.0 kcal/mol.

fields.label: Fail criterion
fields.value: Pre-registered. Refutes the premise if the sensitivity control passes and either AAA ddG >= 2.0 kcal/mol or heterotetramer ipTM < WT ipTM - 0.20. Inconclusive (reason 'other') if WT ipTM < 0.60 or the sensitivity control gives ddG < 2.0 kcal/mol (assay cannot detect a disrupted interface). Anything else is mixed.

fields.label: Interpretation
fields.value: This tests a premise of the claim, not the claim's phenotype: whether the reagent can do what 'dominant-negative' requires (co-assemble and poison the tetramer). That native HCN2 activity is not needed for brain patterning (levin-2018-hcn2-16), and that rescue needs conductance (levin-2018-hcn2-12), both rest on it. Non-conduction itself is not tested; computational structure predictors are known to be insensitive to pore point mutations, and the paper reports voltage-clamp data for that (Supplementary Fig. 2A).
